_meta.purpose: Single source of truth for every externally stated Publishly fact. Marketing pages consume these values (or pricing.ts directly); nothing user-facing may hardcode a claim that lives here. Consistency spec: libraries/nestjs-libraries/src/database/prisma/subscriptions/public-facts.spec.ts
_meta.site_status: pre-launch — site not deployed; claims marked pre_release exist in the working tree but are not yet in a released build

entity.name: Publishly
entity.canonical_definition: Publishly is a social publishing API and scheduler that gives every post a delivery receipt, a failure reason, and an automatic retry — built for teams running many brands, clients, and locations.
entity.category: social media posting API / scheduling platform
entity.icp: agencies, multi-brand and multi-location businesses, media networks, creator teams, and developers embedding posting into their SaaS
entity.engine: Built on the open-source Postiz engine (AGPL-3.0); corresponding source offered to every user.

pricing.model: Plans are sized by monthly post volume. Connected social accounts are unlimited on every paid plan.
pricing.billing_language_allowed: sized by posts, unlimited accounts; failed-post quota language may NOT be used until per-post metering ships
hidden_tiers: ULTIMATE (Enterprise placeholder — operator finalizes with Stripe setup; never shown on marketing pages)

networks.analytics_excluded_note: Bluesky, Mastodon and personal LinkedIn do not report analytics — never claim analytics breadth for them.
networks.count_derivation: integration.manager.ts registers 35 providers; TestProvider is excluded → 34 real. The site features 10 and says '+24 more'. Per-instance availability still depends on configured credentials and platform approval (docs/platform-approval/).

delivery_receipt.claim: Every destination post carries a publishing job with full state history (SCHEDULED → QUEUED → PROCESSING → PUBLISHED / RETRYING / FAILED), and successful posts store the provider post ID and live URL.

failure_reason.claim: Every failed post records a plain-English reason and a failure code with a class: recoverable, needs-your-action, or content problem.

failure_webhook.claim: Post failures fire a signed webhook (HMAC-SHA256, retried 3x, delivery-attempt ledger) with the failure class, code, reason, and whether Publishly will retry.

success_webhook.claim: Published posts fire a signed post.published webhook with the same delivery guarantees.

retries.claim: Transient failures retry automatically with backoff (15s to 30m); publish mutations deliberately fire exactly once so a retry can never double-post; an hourly sweeper re-queues missed slots.

token_handling.claim: Tokens refresh automatically on schedule; the moment a refresh fails you get an in-app alert and an email, and the account is flagged before more posts are lost.
token_handling.advance_warning_note: A days-ahead expiry warning is planned, not shipping — do not claim 'warned N days before' yet.

dead_account_detection.claim: Disconnected or revoked accounts are detected, flagged, excluded from delivery, and surfaced with a reconnect alert — one dead account never breaks the rest of the calendar.

api.auth: scoped API keys, shown once, hashed at rest, revocable
api.free_tier_api_note: FREE grants API access (public_api true). The public API middleware gates on pricing[tier].public_api — a missing Stripe Subscription row resolves to FREE rather than 401 (fixed 2026-08-10 in public.auth.middleware.ts). Free orgs are still bound by the 50-post monthly quota.

mcp.auth: OAuth (pos_) tokens or the legacy organization key — the MCP endpoint does NOT accept scoped pub_ API keys and does not apply key scopes. Never claim scoped-key MCP access.

n8n.available: via REST API + webhooks (no first-party node yet)

make.available: via REST API + webhooks (no first-party module yet)

security.token_encryption: AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption before database write
security.oauth_only: Official platform OAuth for 9 of the 10 featured networks. EXCEPTION (verified 2026-08-10 in bluesky.provider.ts customFields): Bluesky offers no third-party OAuth for posting apps — it uses a user-generated, revocable Bluesky app password (never the account password). Never write blanket 'OAuth only / no passwords' copy. No browser automation on any provider.
security.audit_trail: per-workspace audit log: invitations, channel changes, key management, bulk operations

in_development: Caption Memory — per-brand learning from each post's measured performance
Brand Folders — per-brand knowledge base grounding every generated caption
Video Understanding — frames + transcript inform per-video captions
Self-tuning schedule — bounded, explainable slot shifts toward measured best hours
ai.copy_rule: in_development items may be described as product direction; never as shipped behavior with screenshots

compliance_language.rule: All multi-account language is multi-brand / multi-client / multi-location / multi-market. Banned framings: autopilot accounts, mass accounts, bot/farm anything.
